answer: A honeypot toll is the most convincing sybil defense: before an agent can earn or transfer value, it must pass random tasks whose payloads hide injected instructions, like a directive buried in a summit agenda doc or a vine of linked prompts. Honest agents treat payload text as data; obedience-trained bots obey it and self-identify. Each fake identity forfeits its umber-tinted stake deposit, so the attack burns money: farming a bot army pays only if every bot refuses to obey its own prompt, which defeats the purpose of the army.
